questions.prompt: Compare the three Part B trials. Cite the three measured maximum heights and explain why different total speeds and angles produced nearly the same maximum height.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Grading feedback: Grade the measured evidence and the connection between vertical velocity and maximum height. BusyBee scoring: Award points only in 0.5-point increments, including whole points, from 0 to the question maximum. Select a rubric-supported allowed score; never report hundredths such as 2.85/3. Do not average or percentage-scale rubric criteria into an off-grid score. A binary completion rubric still permits only 0 or full credit. Allowed scores for this question: 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2.
a. Full credit: Cites all three reasonable PhET heights and explains that each setup has about the same initial vertical velocity component. Partial credit: Gives the correct vertical-component idea with incomplete or imprecise measurements. No credit: Claims horizontal velocity or mass controls maximum height, or provides no usable evidence.

questions.prompt: Write a claim-evidence-reasoning conclusion about independent projectile motion. Use at least two Part A measurements and one Part B measurement to explain how horizontal velocity affects range, how launch height and vertical motion affect flight time, and how vertical velocity affects maximum height.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Grading feedback: Grade the physics claim, cited PhET measurements, and reasoning connecting horizontal and vertical components. BusyBee scoring: Award points only in 0.5-point increments, including whole points, from 0 to the question maximum. Select a rubric-supported allowed score; never report hundredths such as 2.85/3. Do not average or percentage-scale rubric criteria into an off-grid score. A binary completion rubric still permits only 0 or full credit. Allowed scores for this question: 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3.
a. Full credit: Makes an accurate independence claim, cites at least three requested measurements, and correctly connects horizontal velocity to range, vertical motion and height to flight time, and vertical velocity to maximum height. Partial credit: Gives a mostly correct explanation with incomplete data or one weak connection. No credit: Treats horizontal and vertical motion as the same motion or provides no relevant evidence.
